answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB is immediate, but promotional_pricing is contraindicated by exp_73 (strong acquisition, -12% retention). The durable memory shows activation_messaging (memory_91) and onboarding simplification (memory_31, memory_86) both improved early engagement and retention without the renewal-cycle collapse observed with discounting. In a churn-defense scenario, improving perceived value and time-to-value through better activation messaging and streamlined onboarding preserves higher-quality retention than matching price cuts. This also avoids training the SMB base to expect discounts. A standard experiment scope allows rapid deployment to defend at-risk segments while measuring retention outcomes. Enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) targets different segments. Referral_incentive (memory_57) works on established customers, not acquisition/churn defense. The activation + onboarding combination addresses root drivers of churn (slow time-to-value, unclear value realization) rather than competing on price, aligning with the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
